items.title: Charles Davis interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 23, 1997
items.q: Well we’re still playing what’s given to us through the “bible” of bebop. Dizzy Gillespie and Charlie Parker and Fats Navarro and Kenny Dorham. I think this is — I don’t know if I’m playing it that well but this is what I’m attempting to do.

ctx.x: Could you describe the style of jazz you play? We were talking just now about labels, trying to put labels on things, and is it possible what you and Joe played last night, what you play down at Small’s when you visit the jam sessions there?

Well we’re still playing what’s given to us through the “bible” of bebop. Dizzy Gillespie and Charlie Parker and Fats Navarro and Kenny Dorham. I think this is — I don’t know if I’m playing it that well but this is what I’m attempting to do.
Would you consider bebop the hardest kind of jazz to play?
